q-130437.name: Question 1
q-130437.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14192268/assets/a3af5c931067f960d2099efdb9a19e23dd2835a16095cdc0e61a0a507b0e8a3c.png)

What is the domain of the function $f$ defined by the mapping diagram above?
q-130437.worked_solution:
The domain is the set of all input values for which the function is defined. In the mapping diagram, this corresponds to the set of values in the "Input" set:

$$
\{5,10,15,20\}
$$

q-6734.name: Question 3
q-6734.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14192268/assets/4091e1bee1b036185a54499839b356f8fce38e864d8f390915e855b26130e998.png)

What is the domain of the function $f(x)$ given above?
q-6734.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ above is defined for values between $x=1$ and $x=4.$

- Since there is a closed circle at $x=1,$ this point is included in the domain.

- On the other hand, because there is an open circle at $x=4,$ this point is not included in the domain.

Therefore, the domain of this function is

$$
1\le x<4.
$$

Using interval notation, we write this as

$$
x\in [1,4).
$$

x∈[1,4).

x=−1

EXPLANATION

The function above is defined for all values of x other than x=−1.
